title: The Two Fundamental Roots
author: Annotated by Zhiyu
excerpt: [All sentient beings, from the beginningless eon, birth and death following in unbroken succession, are all because they do not know the abiding true mind, the pure, bright substance of its nature, but put to use all their delusive thoughts; and because these thoughts are not true, there is the wheel of turning.]

blocks.text: The Unbroken Continuity of Birth and Death

inline.s: [All sentient beings, from the beginningless eon, birth and death following in unbroken succession, are all because they do not know the abiding true mind, the pure, bright substance of its nature, but put to use all their delusive thoughts; and because these thoughts are not true, there is the wheel of turning.]
In the Śūraṅgama Sutra, the World-Honored One teaches: all sentient beings, from the beginningless

. [The pure, bright substance of the nature (xing jing ming ti)] The clear and wonderful substance, pure of nature. [The pure, bright substance of the nature of the true mind (zhen xin xing jing ming ti)]
The nature is the substance, and the mind is the function. The true nature is the substance of the true mind, and the true mind is the function of the true nature.

[Putting to use delusive thoughts (yong zhu wangxiang)] Applying [the mind] to delusive thoughts. Here “zhu” is the combined sound of “zhi yu” (put into). For example: casting it into the shore of the Bohai Sea. [The reality of all dharmas (zhufa shixiang)] The actual state of all dharmas. See further

for details. [Subjection birth and death (fenduan shengsi)] Sentient beings in the six realms of the three worlds, because of what their wholesome and unwholesome karmas have brought, have a fixed limit to their lifespan and a fixed division of their bodily form; hence their birth and death is called “subjection birth and death.” One who ends subjection birth and death escapes the wheel of rebirth and leaves the three worlds. [Trans-formative birth and death (bianyi shengsi)] The sages of the three vehicles have cut off the delusions of view and thought and ended subjection birth and death. In the process of the Way, delusive thought gradually ceases and realizing gradually increases; this transition of delusion and awakening differs in each period. The movement from an earlier period to a later one is like a single episode of birth and death, hence it is called “trans-formative birth and death.” One who ends trans-formative birth and death fully realizes the fruit of Buddhahood.

In the Śūraṅgama Sutra, the World-Honored One reveals two kinds of fundamental root: first, the root of birth and death, namely the seizing mind (the consciousness-mind) that sentient beings employ; second, the root of Buddhahood, namely the originally pure substance (the true nature) realized by the Buddhas.

All sentient beings, from the beginningless eon, with all kinds of inversion, karmic seeds naturally, like the akuña fruits clustered together. The various cultivators are unable to accomplish unexcelled bodhi, and even turn into śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, or become externalists, gods, Mara kings, and Mara's retinue — all because they do not know the two kinds of fundamental root and cultivate confusedly. It is like cooking sand, wishing to make a fine meal
; though one pass through kalpas as many as dust motes, in the end one cannot obtain it.

bitter fruits. [The akuña fruits clustered together (e cha ju)] Akuña
three kernels on a single stem,

when they fall to the ground they mostly gather in one place, hence called “akuña fruits clustered together,” used as a metaphor that delusion, karma, and suffering are interrelated. [Delusion, karma, and suffering (huo, ye, ku)] The causal relation among these three is: because of delusion one creates karma, and because of karma one experiences suffering. That is, due to the delusions of greed, anger, and delusion (cause), one creates all kinds of karma (effect), and again this karma as cause brings on the bitter fruits of birth and death in the three worlds. [Śrāvaka (shengwen)] One who hears the sound of the Buddha speaking of the Four Noble Truths and awakens to the truth. [The Four Noble Truths (si shengdi)] The truth of suffering, the truth of accumulation, the truth of cessation, and the truth of the path. First, the “Truth of Suffering” is the truth that explains the manifold suffering of life. Second, the “collection” in the “Truth of Accumulation” means attracting and creating — it is the truth that explains how the suffering of life comes about. The suffering of life is due to craving and love; whereupon one clings and grasps; whereupon one creates karma; whereupon one suffers; whereupon one transmigrates. Third, the “Truth of Cessation” is the truth that explains the extinction of all suffering. When all the accumulation of suffering (craving and love) is forever cut off without remainder, and there is no grasping or clinging, one no longer creates karma, suffers, or transmigrates — this is the Truth of Cessation. Fourth, the “Truth of the Path” is the truth that explains how to forever cut off the accumulation of suffering (craving and love), that is, the path that extinguishes suffering. Among the Four Noble Truths, accumulation is the cause and suffering the effect; the path is the cause and cessation the effect.

[Pratyekabuddha (yuanjue)] Also called a solitary adept, or pratyeka-buddha. One who, in a Buddha's world, hears the Buddha speak the principle of the twelve links of dependent arising and awakens to the truth is called a “conditioned-awakened one”; one who, born in a world without a Buddha, contemplates the arising and ceasing of all dharmas and conditions and awakens to the truth by himself is called a “solely awakened one.” [Like cooking sand, wishing to make a fine meal]
A metaphor for an impossible thing. That is, what is commonly said — that cooking sand cannot become rice, and grinding a brick cannot make a mirror.

[The dust-point kalpa (chen jie)] Refers to the three-thousand dust-point kalpas, that is, grinding everything in one great thousandfold world-system into ink, and for each great thousandfold world-system passed, dropping one point; when the ink
used up, and all the world-systems passed are again crushed into fine dust, and then each fine dust counted as a kalpa — this is

an extremely long time. [The great thousandfold world-system (daqian shijie)] A thousand small world-systems form a “small thousandfold world-system”; a thousand small thousandfold world-systems form a “middle thousandfold world-system”; a thousand middle thousandfold world-systems form a “great thousandfold world-system.” Because there are three multiples of a thousand in the midst of it, the great thousandfold world-system is also called the “three-thousand-great-thousandfold world-system.”

Next, the World-Honored One reveals two kinds of fundamental root: first, the root of birth and death (the seizing mind); second, the root of the fruit of the bodhi path (the originally pure substance). The seizing mind is false; the originally pure substance is true; cultivation is to return from the false to the true.
What are the two kinds? Ānanda
The first is the beginningless root of birth and death, namely that you now and all sentient beings take the seizing mind as one's own nature.
your own nature, letting it be master

Also called the deliberating mind; this is the mind that arises by seizing upon the six dusts, and is also called the consciousness-mind, the deluded state of the mind. Its characteristic is discriminating reckoning and delighting in and rejecting, taking and letting go. The arising of thought and the functioning of mind, seeing and hearing and perceiving and knowing (here “knowing” is discriminating knowing) — all of these are the consciousness-mind at work. “All sentient beings, from the beginningless eon, birth and death following in unbroken succession, are all because they do not know the abiding true mind, the pure bright substance of its nature
(all because they do not know the pure, bright substance of the nature that abides in the true mind)
, but put to use all these delusive thoughts
(that is, they go on to use delusive thoughts)
; and because these thoughts are not true, there is the wheel of turning.”

The second is the beginningless bodhi, the originally pure substance of nirvāṇa, namely that you now have the originally bright essence of consciousness, which can produce the various conditions, yet is lost among these conditions. Because all sentient beings have lost this original brightness, although they act all day long, they are unaware of it, and vainly enter the various realms.
that is, the originally pure substance of still extinction (nirvāṇa), the true nature. And you now have the originally bright essence of consciousness

, that is, the consciousness-nature. (Regarding the true nature and the consciousness-nature, see further
